External ``-sourced SVGs can't inherit page `currentColor`/CSS variables, which is why the site instead paints a theme-colored dot via a CSS `::after` mask overlay — so recoloring the actual SVG isn't feasible without a much larger rendering rework (inlining every locale's wordmark and touching vendored brand assets), and the assets are documented as vendored, not meant for hand editing. Fixed the overlay's positioning instead, in [pantoken.css](docs/.vitepress/theme/pantoken.css#L254): - The old CSS hardcoded one mask (viewBox + circle) and one width formula from the *default* English wordmark, then just flip-positioned it for `dir="rtl"`. That's wrong for every locale with its own wordmark (`el`, `ar`, `fa`, `he`, `hi`, `hy`, `ja`, `ko`, `ru`, `th`, `uk`, `zh-Hans`/`zh-Hant`), since each has a different aspect ratio and dot position — and none of the RTL locales (ar/fa/he) even use the default logo, so the old RTL rule never applied correctly. - Replaced the hardcoded width/position math with `inset: 0` (the pseudo-element now exactly covers the rendered ``, whatever its aspect ratio) and a `--pantoken-logo-mask` custom property holding a mask SVG built from each wordmark's own `viewBox`/circle coordinates, set per `html[lang="…"]`. Removed the now-unnecessary RTL flip rule. Verified with `vp check` (formatting + lint clean across the docs package).
